recipes.name: The Real Mojito
ingredients_raw: 0.5 medium lime, cut into 3 wedges, divided
2 tablespoons white sugar, or to taste
1 cup ice cubes, or as needed
0.5 cup club soda, or as needed

steps.text: Place mint leaves and 1 lime wedge into a sturdy glass. Use a muddler and crush to release mint oils and lime juice.
Add remaining 2 lime wedges and 2 tablespoons sugar; muddle again to release lime juice. Do not strain mixture.
Fill the glass almost to the top with ice.
Pour in rum and fill the glass with club soda.
Stir, taste, and add more sugar if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: The Real Mojito
raw_recipe.description: Considered Cuba’s national drink, this mojito cocktail is a favorite with pirates, swashbucklers, and colorful characters in the Caribbean and beyond.

video.description: The cocktail recipe in this video is an authentic mojito recipe. It's sized for one serving, but you can adjust it accordingly and make a pitcher full. It's a very refreshing drink for hot summer days. Be careful when drinking it, however.

review.reviewBody:
Good recipe as is.

If I'm going to make several of these, I will make a simple syrup (1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup water, simmered for a few minutes and cooled) and use a few tablespoons of that instead of the sugar. This helps to ensure that the sugar is fully dissolved into the drink. Adds another step, but worth it for company.

This is one of the better mojitos we've had. Maybe not the absolute best (nothing a little tinkering won't fix), but for a DIY mojito, it definitely gets the job nicely done! The husman (too old for "boyfriend," but not married) and I are doing a weekly "cocktail night" and this was the featured cocktail we experimented with for Cocktail Night #2. Solid recipe for this drink. I've had way worse at actual restaurants. 
oh, we used: Puerto Angel white rum, 12 mint leaves per drink, and muddled the heck out of the first 3 ingredients! 

Cheers!

In place of some of the sugar I make a simple MINT syrup by boiling 1 cup of sugar and one cup of water. Once it boils and sugar dissolves add 4 sprgs of mint, remove from heat and cover for an hour. After an hour, strain out the mint and yu are left with a lovely syrup that will add depth to your drink! I also freeze this and use it when needed. I will always add a bit more mint if I have it on hand..so good!

I made these twice. The first time I poured the sugar straight in, but it pooled and barely dissolved no matter how slow i went or how much I stirred. Second time I added an extra step and made simple syrup which went a really long way and really made them perfect!

I followed on of the reviews and made a simple syrup to add instead of sugar, and found it perfect. Before I made this recipe, I had also done some research on Mojito´s and found one great tip online, saying not to add lime wedges since the bitter flavor from the shell would come into the drink, so I juiced the lime instead. I made this in a mason jar, so I doubled the recipe, and because I juiced the lime, I used the juice from 1.5 lime, 3 tbs simple syrup and then followed the recipe for the mint, ice, rum and club soda. 
The mojito turned out a little to strong for my liking, so after drinking a little bit, I then added a little bit more club soda and then it was perfect for me. 
I would probably add 1 ounce of rum next time (in my case 2 ounces since I double it) so it wont become to strong.

I love me a good mojito. Mirrors taste great and are so refreshing. 

I did like this recipe, but had to make quite a few tweaks to be up to my preference. First, I did make a simple syrup. 1 cup sugar to 1 cup water. If you make a big pitcher, you will need a lot of simple syrup. Second, I added more rum than mentioned. Third, I strained some of the pulp from the lime. 

Instead of the sugar, put some simple syrup and muddle the lime and mint. This makes it a bit tastier. 

Serve over ice, with lime and mint as a garnish.

I have been to Cuba and there they fill the glass with mint and then add the liquids. A lot more rum too. My go to recipe is to fill the glass with fresh mint leaves, then make up this mixture: first make 1 cup of simple syrup by boiling 3/4 cup sugar with 3/4 cup water. Then add 2 cups light Cuban rum and 1 1/4 cups fresh lime juice. Fill glasses 1/3 full, then add ice cubes and soda water to fill the glass. Add a straw to muddle.
I made enough for 4 servings; in a pitcher. Once I muddled the mint leaves, sugar and lime, I added to a pitcher. Added ice, then the 3\4 c Bacardi Light Rum and 1 liter of club soda. It was perfect!
I had fresh picked blueberries so, added 1/4 cup blueberries and squeezed half of the lime juice and muddled with the mint leaves. Then added rum and sugar. Too with club soda Delicious!

Very Good! Mint and lime make for a perfect summer cocktail. If you are looking for a slightly sweeter/simpler version forgo the sugar v simple syrup debate and substitute Sprite/7up or other lemon-lime soda for the club soda and sugar. Also another *hint* can put together rum lime and mint earlier in the day and then strain for a flavor boost using fresh mint for garnish.

This was so good! I used sugar cubes, because it was the only sugar I had in the bar, and had them mostly melt in the bottom of the glass (because sugar cubes are pretty hard). It was a great way to control the sweetness. I just lifted or lowered my straw a little. Since you can't really drink to the bottom anyway without sucking up mashed up mint and lime wedges, this worked perfectly for me. I used 4 sugar cubes, muddling 3 with the mint and lime. Perfect.
Not sweet enough and with 2 T of sugar I didn’t want to add more. I’ll try simple syrup next time to satisfy need for sweet.
No I loved it just the way it is
This was delicious! We chose to add some simple syrup to meet our sweetness level. Then he asked for a second. Then he asked what he needed to keep on hand to have those again!

Amazing recipe! One of my Cuban friends said it’s the best mojito they’ve ever had. I kept the sugar, rather than using simple syrup, since it keeps the freshness. I even went as far as to add a third tablespoon of sugar for those that hate the taste of alcohol
Good recipe. Probably doesn’t need quite to much sugar, and I used crushed ice.
Took advice of others and used half the amount cane sugar instead of regular. Absolutely perfect!
